hero.headline: Daveigh Chase, voice of Lilo and star of The Ring, dies at 35
hero.body:
Daveigh Chase, the actress who voiced the title character in Disney's Lilo & Stitch and starred as the vengeful ghost Samara in the 2002 horror film The Ring, has died at age 35. She died from meningitis and blood infections that developed into sepsis, according to her boyfriend Roy Hernandez.

Chase became a household name in the early 2000s through two distinctly different roles. She provided the voice of Lilo Pelekai, the spirited young Hawaiian girl at the center of Disney's 2002 animated feature Lilo & Stitch. That same year, she portrayed Samara Morgan in The Ring, Gore Verbinski's English-language remake of the Japanese horror film Ringu. Her performance as the long-haired ghost who emerges from a television set helped make The Ring one of the highest-grossing horror remakes in history.

Born on July 24, 1990, in Las Vegas, Nevada, Chase began her career as a child actress. Beyond her most famous roles, she appeared in the cult film Donnie Darko and had roles in Sabrina the Teenage Witch. She also voiced Chihiro Ogino in the English dub of Studio Ghibli's Spirited Away. Chase continued working in voice acting throughout her career, reprising the role of Lilo in various Lilo & Stitch sequels and spinoffs.

Chase's dual success in both family entertainment and horror made her a unique figure in Hollywood. The contrast between her warm, energetic voice work as Lilo and her unsettling portrayal of Samara showcased her range as a performer.

According to Hernandez, Chase had been admitted to a Los Angeles hospital earlier this month due to malnutrition before her condition worsened. In a GoFundMe page set up before her death, Hernandez described her struggles behind the scenes. "After a difficult childhood and a painful falling out with her family, Daveigh was bullied and struggled to find safety and happiness in downtown LA," he wrote. He added that he had promised to protect her and give her the love and comfort she deserved.

"Recently, everything changed. Daveigh was diagnosed with meningitis and several serious blood infections. Her condition has become critical, and the doctors have told me she may not have much time left," Hernandez said on the fundraising page, which had raised $1,300 of its $5,500 goal as of Wednesday evening.

News of her death spread rapidly across entertainment media, with tributes noting her impact on both Disney animation fans and horror enthusiasts.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran Sign Initial Agreement to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
cards.body:
The United States and Iran have signed a preliminary agreement aimed at ending their conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping waterway that handles roughly one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas. The 14-paragraph memo includes an end to fighting, a commitment that Iran will never develop nuclear weapons, and a $300 billion redevelopment package for Iran. Oil prices fell immediately following the announcement as markets anticipated the resumption of tanker traffic through the strait.

The agreement marks a significant diplomatic breakthrough after weeks of military confrontation and represents the first major step toward de-escalation. Both governments signed the document, though the path forward remains complicated by disagreements on deeper issues. Negotiators from both sides acknowledged that more difficult negotiations lie ahead as they work toward a comprehensive peace settlement.

The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has created a spiralling global economic crisis. The closure forced tankers to take longer routes and stranded approximately 20,000 seafarers and 2,000 ships in the Gulf region. Countries dependent on imported oil have been hit particularly hard, with shortages affecting fuel, fertilizer, and other raw materials. Germany halved its 2026 growth forecast to 0.5 percent, while Greece announced 500 million euros in additional support for households and farmers.

Despite the agreement's promise, significant obstacles remain. Regional allies have expressed concern about the deal's limited scope. Gulf states reportedly remain frustrated that the agreement does not address Iranian missile and drone capabilities, which have been central to regional security concerns. Israeli officials also voiced disappointment, saying the agreement accomplishes none of Israel's stated war aims and arguably leaves the country in worse shape on each of them.

Iran's parliament speaker and lead negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has raised doubts about whether the agreement will hold. He stated that reopening the strait would be "impossible" while the U.S. and Israel continued what he described as breaches of the ceasefire, including a U.S. naval blockade. Iran has also seized two ships in the strait and accused them of attempting to exit covertly, marking the first time Iran has taken control of vessels since the conflict began on February 28.

The initial agreement comes as the Trump administration faces record low approval ratings according to a new poll. The president put pressure on Iran to end its blockade but later imposed his own blockade when those efforts failed, contributing to additional fuel price hikes and threats of long-term inflation.

Pakistan acted as mediator in the negotiations, with plans for talks scheduled in Islamabad. However, Iranian negotiators never publicly accepted the invitation, and the U.S. delegation led by Vice President JD Vance never left Washington, leaving uncertainty about whether diplomatic momentum can be sustained for a final settlement.

cards.headline: Ukraine Launches Major Drone Attack on Moscow Refinery
cards.teaser: Ukrainian forces struck a refinery in the Russian capital, forcing airport closures for several hours.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck multiple locations across Moscow in the largest air raid on the city since Russia's full-scale invasion began. Nearly 200 drones hit an area southeast of the capital, setting a major oil refinery and a shopping centre ablaze. Authorities forced evacuations at Russia's largest airport as a security measure during the assault.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy characterized the attack as retaliation for Russia's strike on the Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, a historic monastery complex, earlier that week. The operation represented a significant escalation in Ukraine's campaign against Russian energy infrastructure targets.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Interest Rates Steady Under New Chairman Warsh
cards.teaser: Kevin Warsh opted against providing policy guidance at his first meeting as Federal Reserve chairman, leaving markets uncertain about future rate moves.
cards.body:
The Federal Reserve maintained interest rates at 3.5% to 3.75% during its first meeting under new chairman Kevin Warsh. The decision received unanimous support from the Fed's voting committee, which noted that economic activity is expanding at a solid pace.

Warsh has signaled a shift in how the central bank communicates with markets, providing less forward guidance than his predecessors. This change in strategy has prompted futures markets to price in at least one rate increase before year's end, reflecting investor expectations that Warsh will prioritize fighting inflation.

cards.headline: Waymo recalls 4,000 robotaxis after vehicles entered highway construction zones
cards.body:
Waymo has issued a recall affecting nearly 4,000 of its autonomous vehicles after identifying instances where the robotaxis drove into highway sections closed for construction. The company documented at least 13 separate incidents where its self-driving cars entered restricted construction areas on highways.

The recall addresses a software issue that prevented the vehicles from properly recognizing and responding to highway construction zone closures. Waymo's autonomous driving system failed to interpret the temporary road restrictions, allowing the robotaxis to proceed into areas where construction work was actively taking place. The company has not disclosed whether any of these incidents resulted in accidents, injuries, or property damage.

Waymo operates one of the largest commercial robotaxi fleets in the United States, providing ride-hailing services in several cities. The recall represents a significant portion of the company's active fleet and will require a software update to correct the navigation system's ability to detect and avoid construction zones. The fix aims to improve how the vehicles process temporary road closures and construction signage.

The recall comes as autonomous vehicle companies face increased scrutiny over safety performance. Self-driving technology relies on a combination of sensors, cameras, and mapping data to navigate roads, but temporary changes like construction zones can present unique challenges. Unlike permanent road features that can be pre-mapped, construction zones often appear suddenly and may not be reflected in existing digital maps.

Waymo has not provided a specific timeline for completing the software updates across its fleet. The company continues to operate its robotaxi service while implementing the fix. This recall follows other recent safety actions in the autonomous vehicle industry as regulators and companies work to address the challenges of deploying self-driving cars at scale on public roads.

cards.headline: San Andreas fault reaches highest stress levels in 1,000 years
cards.teaser: Scientists warn that California's San Andreas fault has built up more stress than at any point in the last millennium, raising concerns about a major earthquake.
cards.body:
Research shows that the San Andreas fault, which runs through California, has accumulated stress levels higher than any point in the past 1,000 years. Scientists studying historical stress patterns have determined that this buildup increases seismic risk across the region.

When geological faults accumulate stress over extended periods, they eventually rupture and release that energy as earthquakes. California's location on the boundary between major tectonic plates makes it particularly vulnerable to significant earthquakes when this accumulated stress is finally released.

cards.headline: Trump economic approval hits new low, trailing Biden's worst rating
cards.teaser: A new poll shows President Trump's economic approval at 33 percent, three points below former President Biden's lowest mark during his administration.
cards.body:
President Trump's approval rating for his handling of the economy has reached 33 percent, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. This marks his lowest economic approval rating since taking office.

The figure is three percentage points below the lowest approval rating former President Biden received on economic matters during his presidency, when he hit 36 percent approval.

cards.headline: Defense Secretary Criticizes NATO Allies Over Iran War Response
cards.teaser: Pete Hegseth called European military support during the U.S.-Iran conflict inadequate at a NATO defense ministers meeting.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth criticized European NATO allies at a defense ministers meeting, calling their response to the U.S. war with Iran "shameful." He announced that the United States would review its force commitments in Europe, warning that some allies would fail to meet expectations.

The Pentagon is scaling back American commitments to a high-readiness force within NATO, signaling a shift in U.S.-European defense cooperation. Meanwhile, the Iran conflict is affecting civilians globally, driving up oil prices and increasing costs for household energy and food.

cards.headline: Israel Voices Disappointment with U.S.-Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Israeli officials said the preliminary peace deal fails to achieve any of the country's stated objectives from the conflict.
cards.body:
Israel expressed strong disappointment with the U.S.-Iran preliminary agreement, saying it fails to achieve any of the country's stated war objectives. Israeli officials argued the deal leaves them in a worse strategic position on each of their key goals.

The agreement includes an end to fighting, a commitment that Iran will never develop nuclear weapons, and a $300 billion redevelopment package for Iran. It also reopens the Strait of Hormuz for shipping. However, Israeli leaders had hoped the conflict would result in stricter limits on Iranian military capabilities and regional influence—neither of which the initial accord addresses.

cards.headline: Gulf States Question U.S. Security Guarantees After Iran Deal
cards.teaser: Regional powers expressed concern that the preliminary agreement does not address Iranian missiles and drones.
cards.body:
Gulf states voiced frustration that the U.S.-Iran peace deal fails to address Iranian rocket and drone capabilities, according to analysts. The omission has raised questions in the region about the reliability of Washington as a security guarantor.

Iranian missiles and drones have been a central concern for Gulf nations throughout the conflict. The preliminary agreement's focus on reopening shipping lanes without constraining these weapons systems has left regional allies uncertain about future security arrangements.

cards.headline: UK By-Election in Makerfield Could Determine Prime Minister's Future
cards.teaser: Voters head to polls in a contest that could lead to Keir Starmer's removal as prime minister.
cards.body:
A by-election taking place in Makerfield carries major consequences for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's political future. The outcome of the vote could potentially lead to Starmer's ouster as head of government.

The contest has drawn national attention because of its potential impact on Labour Party leadership. A loss in the traditionally held seat could trigger a confidence crisis within the party and force a leadership challenge against the prime minister.

cards.headline: Southeast Asia Turns to Solar Power Amid Energy Crisis
cards.teaser: Homeowners and businesses are installing rooftop panels to offset soaring energy costs caused by the Iran war.
cards.body:
Residents and businesses across Southeast Asia are installing rooftop solar panels at an accelerated pace to cope with rising energy costs triggered by the Iran war. The region, which relies heavily on imported oil, has seen energy prices surge since the conflict disrupted global oil markets.

The shift to solar power offers households and companies relief from the financial strain of elevated fuel costs. The energy crisis has made renewable installations more economically attractive, spurring faster adoption of solar technology throughout the region.

hero.headline: Tropical Storm Arthur brings flooding threat to Southeast
hero.body:
Tropical Storm Arthur, the first named storm of the Atlantic hurricane season, moved across the Southeast on Thursday after making landfall along the upper Texas coast. The system weakened from a cyclone to a low pressure area as it lost wind intensity, with maximum sustained winds around 35 mph.

Despite its downgrade, forecasters warned that Arthur still posed life-threatening flooding risks across multiple states. The primary threat came from prolonged, heavy rainfall expected to continue through Friday. According to the National Hurricane Center, Arthur could produce 5 to 10 inches of rain across affected areas, with some isolated locations potentially receiving up to 20 inches.

"The main threat from Arthur is going to be a prolonged, multiday, heavy rainfall event that could produce dangerous to life-threatening flash flooding," said National Hurricane Center director Michael Brennan.

The highest flood risk was expected to shift eastward throughout the week, beginning in Texas and Louisiana before moving into Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia and the Florida panhandle. A High Risk for Excessive Rainfall was issued for portions of the Central Gulf Coast, a designation that indicates potential for both widespread and life-threatening flash flooding.

All coastal watches and warnings were discontinued on Wednesday, but flooding remained likely through Friday across Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Georgia and the Florida panhandle. Some communities in Louisiana and Mississippi took precautionary measures by distributing sandbags to residents and clearing debris from drainage systems ahead of the storm's arrival.

AccuWeather Vice President of Forecast Operations Dan DePodwin noted that "a significant flood risk exists each day this week, shifting slowly eastward from Texas into Wednesday to Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and Georgia during the second half of the week."

Beyond flooding concerns, forecasters warned of additional threats from the storm system. Swells generated by Arthur were expected to create life-threatening surf and rip-current conditions along the northwestern Gulf Coast over the coming days. Tornados remained possible through Thursday as the storm's remnants moved across Gulf Coast states.

The National Weather Service emphasized the dangers of flood waters, stating "NEVER walk or drive into flood waters. Turn around, don't drown!"

Arthur's early arrival marked an unusual start to the Atlantic hurricane season, which typically peaks in late summer and early fall. Emergency management officials across affected states continued monitoring conditions as the system tracked eastward across the Southeast. Residents in affected areas were advised to monitor local weather updates and avoid flooded roadways as cleanup and assessment efforts began in areas where the storm had already passed.

cards.headline: Algae bloom in Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool reaches highest levels in years
cards.teaser: Green algae blooms have returned to the Reflecting Pool at record intensity, aerial photos show.
cards.body:
The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool has experienced a resurgence of algae blooms, with toxicity levels reaching their highest point in recent years. Aerial photographs captured the pool's water turned distinctly green, highlighting the severity of the current bloom.

The algae problem at the iconic Washington monument site has grown worse despite previous mitigation efforts. Images also showed damage to the South Lawn area near the pool. The toxic algae issue has drawn attention from late night television programs and national media outlets as the bloom expanded.

cards.headline: Seattle shooting death of teen at 2020 racial justice protest remains unsolved
cards.teaser: Antonio Mays Jr., 16, was killed during the Capitol Hill Occupied Protest six years ago.
cards.body:
Sixteen-year-old Antonio Mays Jr. traveled from his home to Seattle in the summer of 2020 to participate in racial justice demonstrations following the killing of George Floyd. He arrived during the Capitol Hill Occupied Protest, an area where protesters established an autonomous zone known as CHOP.

Less than a week after his arrival, Mays was shot and killed within the protest zone. The case has never been solved, and no arrests have been made in connection with his death. A new investigation by NPR, KUOW, and The Seattle Times examines the circumstances surrounding the shooting and the unsolved nature of the case.

cards.headline: Russia's nuclear-powered cruise missile uses dangerous design, researchers say
cards.teaser: MIT analysts believe they have determined how Russia's Burevestnik missile operates.
cards.body:
MIT researchers have analyzed Russia's Burevestnik nuclear-powered cruise missile and determined how the weapon likely operates. The missile, known to NATO as Skyfall, is designed to use nuclear propulsion to extend its range indefinitely.

According to the analysts, the design concept is theoretically feasible but carries significant drawbacks. The nuclear propulsion system creates radiation hazards that make the missile both dirty and dangerous, particularly during testing and deployment phases. Russia has been developing the weapon as part of its strategic arsenal.

cards.headline: Teacher sentenced to life in prison for murdering adopted son
cards.teaser: Jamie Varley subjected Preston Davey to months of physical and sexual abuse before his death.
cards.body:
Jamie Varley, 37, received a whole life prison sentence for the murder of his adopted baby son, Preston Davey. The teacher subjected the child to months of horrific physical, sexual, and emotional abuse before the boy's death.

Varley's actions over an extended period resulted in Preston's death after sustained mistreatment. The court determined that the severity and duration of the abuse warranted the maximum sentence, ensuring Varley will remain in prison for the rest of his life without the possibility of parole.

cards.headline: Refugee players at World Cup campaign for attitude change
cards.teaser: Germany's Antonio Rudiger and others share stories of fleeing conflict zones.
cards.body:
Several World Cup players are using the tournament as a platform to advocate for changing global attitudes toward refugees and displaced persons. Germany's Antonio Rudiger is among them, drawing from his family's experience fleeing Sierra Leone's civil war. During their escape from the violence, Rudiger's brother hid in a rice sack.

These athletes' personal histories as refugees add a human dimension to broader discussions about refugee crises and immigration policy. By speaking out at the World Cup, they aim to shift public perception about people forced to flee war and persecution.

cards.headline: Russian shadow fleet tanker enters English Channel
cards.teaser: The vessel Forwarder is the first such ship to transit the waterway since a recent boarding incident.
cards.body:
A Russian-flagged tanker called Forwarder entered the English Channel on Wednesday evening, becoming the first vessel from Russia's shadow fleet to transit the busy waterway since the boarding of the Smyrtos. The ship departed from Primorsk port the previous week.

Shadow fleet vessels operate outside conventional oversight to evade international sanctions. The Forwarder's passage highlights ongoing scrutiny of Russian maritime activity in western waters.

hero.headline: Gas Prices Drop Below $4 Per Gallon as Iran Deal Eases Oil Supply Concerns
hero.body:
Average gasoline prices across the United States fell below $4 per gallon for the first time in months following a U.S.-Iran agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The decline reflects investor confidence that the critical shipping route will soon resume normal operations after being blocked during the conflict that began on February 28.

Oil prices responded sharply to news of the deal. Brent crude futures, the global oil benchmark, fell to $82 a barrel, down from prices that had soared during the energy crisis. Stock markets rallied on the announcement, with Japan's Nikkei rising nearly 3% and Europe's Stoxx 600 index gaining 1%. The pound strengthened to its highest level since mid-May, while gold climbed 1.46% to $4,574 an ounce.

The Strait of Hormuz serves as a vital chokepoint for global oil shipments, with a substantial portion of the world's petroleum exports flowing through the waterway. Its de facto closure for more than 100 days created the greatest recorded disruption to global energy supplies in recent history. The blockade sent fuel costs soaring worldwide and triggered concerns about prolonged supply constraints.

However, analysts cautioned against excessive optimism. Warren Patterson, head of commodities strategy at ING, told Reuters: "We've been at this stage before, only for talks to break down. Therefore, the market will likely be more cautious about overreacting." Giovanni Staunovo, a UBS analyst, noted that while the agreement offers hope, physical oil flows through the strait remain restricted.

Even with the agreement in place, a full return to normal oil supplies will take time. Analysts expect that damaged energy infrastructure in the region requires months to repair. Wholesale gas prices fell about 6% following the deal announcement, but oil prices remain substantially higher than pre-conflict levels, when Brent crude traded around $70 per barrel.

The agreement addresses broader economic concerns beyond energy markets. Inflation fears have risen significantly due to higher oil and gas costs, as well as increased prices for materials including fertilizer, which is expected to drive food prices higher. The Bank of England held interest rates steady, warning that the Middle East disruption remained a major source of economic uncertainty. Prior to the conflict, central banks anticipated rate cuts, but the energy shock reversed those expectations, with markets now predicting rate increases.

Stephen Innes, an independent analyst, described the market reaction: "The market response made perfect sense given how much inflation fear and hawkish rate pricing had been embedded into the curve during the recent energy shock."

The reopening of the strait could provide relief to household budgets and potentially ease some of the broader inflationary pressures affecting economies worldwide, though energy markets will continue monitoring developments in the Middle East to assess whether supply improvements can be sustained.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Holds Interest Rates Steady Under New Chairman Warsh
cards.teaser: Kevin Warsh opted against providing policy guidance at his first meeting as Federal Reserve chairman, leaving markets uncertain about future rate moves.
cards.body:
The Federal Reserve maintained interest rates at 3.5% to 3.75% during its first meeting under new chairman Kevin Warsh. The decision received unanimous support from the Fed's voting committee, which noted that economic activity is expanding at a solid pace.

Warsh has signaled a shift in how the central bank communicates with markets, providing less forward guidance than his predecessors. This change in strategy has prompted futures markets to price in at least one rate increase before year's end, reflecting investor expectations that Warsh will prioritize fighting inflation.

cards.headline: Bank of England Keeps Interest Rates on Hold Citing Energy Price Uncertainty
cards.teaser: British policymakers maintained current rates, warning that the war in Iran remains a major source of economic uncertainty despite the Hormuz agreement.
cards.body:
The Bank of England maintained interest rates at their current level, citing ongoing uncertainty in the Middle East as a key concern. The central bank last reduced rates in December but has paused further cuts as regional upheaval continues to affect energy markets and economic conditions.

The decision reflects broader economic pressures on UK households and businesses. Retail giant Tesco reported that comparable sales growth slowed to 1.8% in the three months to end May, attributing the decline partly to Middle East-related uncertainty affecting consumer confidence and spending patterns.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Rise After Jobless Claims Report and Hormuz Reopening
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained ground as investors responded positively to employment data and easing oil supply concerns.
cards.body:
Stock markets opened higher after the release of jobless claims data and news of the Strait of Hormuz reopening. The Dow brushed off uncertainty from the Federal Reserve's rate decision and climbed as investors processed multiple economic developments.

Intel shares surged after former President Trump posted about a partnership with Apple, adding to the positive market momentum. Oil prices fell on the Hormuz news, providing additional support to equities. The combination of labor market data and energy price relief helped drive gains across major indexes despite lingering questions about the Fed's policy direction under its new leadership.

cards.headline: Job Vacancies in Britain Fall to Five-Year Low
cards.teaser: The number of open positions dropped to the lowest level in five years, suggesting companies are becoming more cautious about hiring.
cards.body:
British job vacancies fell to their lowest level in five years according to new government figures. The decline indicates that companies are taking a more conservative approach to staffing decisions amid economic uncertainty.

The data suggests businesses are reassessing their hiring needs as they navigate challenges including inflation, energy costs, and interest rate policy. The drop in vacancies could signal a cooling labor market after a period of tight employment conditions. Economists view the trend as evidence that companies are adapting to a more uncertain economic environment by limiting expansion plans.

cards.headline: Qantas Plans Record-Breaking Nonstop Flight Between Sydney and London
cards.teaser: The Australian airline will launch a 22-hour direct service between the two cities, set to become the world's longest commercial flight.
cards.body:
Qantas will launch the world's longest nonstop commercial flight, connecting Sydney and London starting in October next year. The route spans approximately 11,000 miles and will take around 22 hours to complete.

London is the first destination for Qantas's Project Sunrise initiative, designed to link Australia directly to major international cities without stops. The airline has configured special aircraft to support the extended range and duration required for this ultra-long-haul operation.

cards.headline: CrossCountry Named Worst Train Operator in Britain
cards.teaser: The rail company received the lowest ranking from passengers, with Transport Focus calling for improvements in delays and disruption communication.
cards.body:
CrossCountry was ranked as Britain's worst train operator in a new passenger satisfaction survey. Transport Focus, the consumer watchdog, specifically asked the company to reduce delays and provide better information to travelers during service disruptions.

The ranking reflects ongoing complaints about reliability and customer service across the rail network. Transport Focus highlighted that passengers want clearer communication when trains are delayed or canceled. The poor performance comes as the rail industry faces pressure to improve service quality and rebuild ridership following recent disruptions.

cards.headline: Scientists find garnet in Mars meteorite for first time
cards.teaser: Researchers discovered the mineral garnet inside a Martian meteorite, offering new clues about how the red planet evolved billions of years ago.
cards.body:
Scientists have identified garnet in a Mars meteorite for the first time, marking a new discovery that could help explain the geological history of the red planet. The mineral was found when researchers cracked open the meteorite for analysis. The University of Trieste announced the finding, which adds another layer to understanding Mars' geological past.

Garnet forms under specific pressure and temperature conditions, making its presence significant for reconstructing the planet's early environment. The discovery may reveal information about how Mars evolved billions of years ago, when its interior and surface conditions were dramatically different from today. Researchers are analyzing the garnet to piece together the geological processes that shaped the planet during its early history.

cards.headline: San Andreas fault reaches highest stress levels in 1,000 years
cards.teaser: Scientists warn that California's San Andreas fault has built up more stress than at any point in the last millennium, raising concerns about a major earthquake.

cards.headline: Adobe adds AI assistant to Premiere, Illustrator, and InDesign
cards.teaser: Adobe is expanding its Firefly AI assistant with new capabilities and integrating it into Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign, and Frame.io.
cards.body:
Adobe has expanded its Firefly AI assistant to Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign, and Frame.io. The company is updating the tool with new capabilities across these applications, extending AI features to video editing, graphic design, publishing, and team collaboration workflows.

The expansion brings artificial intelligence assistance to a wider range of creative tasks within Adobe's product suite, helping users work more efficiently across different types of projects.

cards.headline: NASA selects Eric Schmidt's rocket company for Mars mission
cards.teaser: NASA has chosen a rocket company founded by Eric Schmidt to participate in a Mars mission, setting up competition with SpaceX.
cards.body:
NASA awarded a contract to a rocket company founded by former Google CEO Eric Schmidt for an upcoming Mars mission. The selection establishes a competitive dynamic with SpaceX, which has dominated NASA's commercial space partnerships in recent years. The Mars mission will involve multiple private sector partners working alongside the space agency.

The contract marks a significant entry for Schmidt's aerospace venture into deep space exploration. NASA has increasingly turned to private companies to develop and operate spacecraft for planetary missions, seeking to reduce costs while expanding capabilities. The Mars mission timeline and specific responsibilities for Schmidt's company were not detailed in the announcement.

cards.headline: Spotify launches Reserved system to hold concert tickets for superfans
cards.teaser: Spotify introduced Reserved, a new feature that sets aside two concert tickets for an artist's most dedicated listeners before public sales begin.
cards.body:
Spotify has launched Reserved, a new ticket reservation system that gives superfans early access to concert tickets. The platform holds two tickets for an artist's most dedicated listeners before general public sales begin, leveraging streaming data to identify fan engagement.

The feature connects Spotify's digital music ecosystem with live event experiences, allowing the company to reward its most active users while creating value for artists and venues. This marks another step in Spotify's broader push into live entertainment and fan experiences beyond music streaming.

cards.headline: Rockstar confirms Grand Theft Auto VI preorder date and cover art
cards.teaser: Rockstar Games revealed the official cover artwork for GTA 6 and announced that preorders will open on June 25.
cards.body:
Rockstar Games has announced that Grand Theft Auto VI preorders will begin on June 25, with PlayStation 5 among the first platforms available. The company revealed the game's final cover art through a viral video released months ahead of the game's launch.

The preorder announcement and cover reveal mark major milestones for one of the gaming industry's most anticipated releases. Grand Theft Auto VI has generated significant global excitement following years of development by Rockstar Games.

hero.headline: Carolina Hurricanes win 2026 Stanley Cup, parade set for Raleigh
hero.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes claimed the 2026 Stanley Cup championship on Sunday, defeating the Vegas Golden Knights 3-0 in Game 6. The victory marks the franchise's second Cup title, exactly 20 years after their first championship in 2006. The team will celebrate with a parade in Raleigh on Saturday, an event officials expect could become one of the largest parades North Carolina has ever seen.

Rod Brind'Amour, the Hurricanes head coach and a Greensboro native, has now won two Stanley Cups with the organization. He won his first as captain in 2006 and has guided the team to another championship as coach. Brind'Amour made his NHL playoff debut in 1989 and joined the Hurricanes in 1997, becoming instrumental in transforming the struggling franchise after it relocated from Hartford.

The Hurricanes' path to the 2026 championship was notably different from their 2006 run. Carolina had repeatedly lost in the Eastern Conference Finals in 2019, 2023, and 2025, raising questions about whether the team could ever advance past those rounds. What changed this year came partly from roster decisions made in spring 2025. After missing out on acquiring Mitch Marner, who joined Vegas, the Hurricanes pivoted by trading Mikko Rantanen to Dallas for Logan Stankoven while securing Nikolaj Ehlers from Winnipeg.

The additions proved crucial. Stankoven and Ehlers combined for significant playoff production, giving Carolina more offensive depth than in previous seasons. During Sunday's clinching game in Vegas, Stankoven's line provided the 2-0 lead that became the decisive margin. Marner, playing for the Golden Knights, finished his first season there with 10 goals and 19 playoff assists, but the Hurricanes' acquired talents ultimately outproduced him when it mattered most.

Jordan Staal, 37, hoisted the Stanley Cup first for Carolina. The captain has been with the organization since 2012 and his relationship with Brind'Amour has been credited as key to the team's success and culture.

The team debuted the Stanley Cup to massive crowds in Raleigh's Glenwood South area after returning home. City officials are urging fans to carpool or use public transportation for Saturday's parade to manage the anticipated record-breaking turnout. Raleigh has published logistics information to help coordinate the celebration, which will draw fans from across the region to honor the Hurricanes' championship victory.

The championship represents a major moment for North Carolina sports, bringing hockey's top prize to a state long dominated by college basketball. It validates the franchise's perseverance through years of playoff disappointment and marks a significant achievement for the fanbase known as Caniacs.

cards.headline: New York Knicks hold championship parade through Manhattan
cards.teaser: The Knicks celebrated their NBA championship with a parade through New York City, with 10,000 police officers deployed for security.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks celebrated their NBA championship with a parade through the Canyon of Heroes in Manhattan, drawing crowds of fans throughout the city. The procession made its way to City Hall as supporters gathered to mark the historic victory.

The NYPD deployed 10,000 officers to manage the event and ensure public safety during the celebration.

cards.headline: Glenn Phillips scores first Test century for New Zealand at The Oval
cards.teaser: New Zealand batsman Glenn Phillips reached his maiden Test hundred against England, helping his side to 391 on day two.
cards.body:
Glenn Phillips marked a milestone with his first Test century for New Zealand during the second Test against England at The Oval. Playing on the second day of the match, Phillips led his team's batting effort as New Zealand reached 391 runs.

The right-hander's innings came amid England's bowling assault, with the hosts deploying a short-ball strategy. Phillips' century proved instrumental in establishing a strong position for the visitors in their first innings.

cards.headline: Ivory Coast forward Elye Wahi denied entry to Canada amid fixing allegations
cards.teaser: World Cup player Elye Wahi was arrested and denied a Canadian visa following allegations of involvement in Ligue 1 spot-fixing offenses.
cards.body:
Ivory Coast forward Elye Wahi has been denied entry to Canada for his team's World Cup match against Germany on Saturday in Toronto. The Ivory Coast football federation announced that the necessary administrative authorizations for Wahi to enter Canadian territory could not be obtained.

Wahi is currently under investigation for alleged fixing offenses related to organized fraud in Ligue 1. His absence means he will miss the fixture as he is unable to travel with the squad.

cards.headline: Ben Stokes returns to Durham after being dropped from England captaincy
cards.teaser: Former England captain Ben Stokes will make his return to cricket for Durham in a County Championship match against Northamptonshire.
cards.body:
Ben Stokes has been named in Durham's squad for their County Championship match against Northamptonshire on Friday, marking his return to action following his departure from the England captaincy.

The all-rounder will play his first match since stepping down from the role, competing in county cricket competition for Durham.

cards.headline: England drawn against Greece in 2027 Women's World Cup play-offs
cards.teaser: The Lionesses will face Greece in the first round of qualifying play-offs for the 2027 Women's World Cup.
cards.body:
England will face Greece in the first round of the 2027 Women's World Cup play-offs. If they win, the Lionesses will advance to face either Slovakia or Ukraine in the next stage.

Scotland drew Czechia in round one and could face Sweden if they progress. Wales have been drawn against Norway, while Northern Ireland will play Iceland if they win their first match. All four home nations are competing in the play-off system to secure spots at the 2027 tournament in Brazil.

cards.headline: Fox World Cup broadcast sees on-air clash between Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Alexi Lalas
cards.teaser: Fox's World Cup coverage featured tensions between pundits Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Alexi Lalas, with Ibrahimovic calling comments ignorant.
cards.body:
Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Alexi Lalas clashed during Fox's World Cup broadcast coverage. Ibrahimovic called Lalas ignorant during on-air commentary, sparking speculation about tension between the pundits.

Thierry Henry also expressed displeasure after Landon Donovan called France arrogant during the World Cup opener. The broadcast disputes have drawn attention to Fox's pundit lineup and commentary approach for the tournament.

hero.headline: Daveigh Chase, voice of Lilo and star of The Ring, dies at 35
hero.body:
Daveigh Chase, the actress who voiced the title character in Disney's Lilo & Stitch and starred as the vengeful ghost Samara in the 2002 horror film The Ring, has died at age 35. She died from meningitis and blood infections that developed into sepsis, according to her boyfriend Roy Hernandez.

Chase became a household name in the early 2000s through two distinctly different roles. She provided the voice of Lilo Pelekai, the spirited young Hawaiian girl at the center of Disney's 2002 animated feature Lilo & Stitch. That same year, she portrayed Samara Morgan in The Ring, Gore Verbinski's English-language remake of the Japanese horror film Ringu. Her performance as the long-haired ghost who emerges from a television set helped make The Ring one of the highest-grossing horror remakes in history.

Born on July 24, 1990, in Las Vegas, Nevada, Chase began her career as a child actress. Beyond her most famous roles, she appeared in the cult film Donnie Darko and had roles in Sabrina the Teenage Witch. She also voiced Chihiro Ogino in the English dub of Studio Ghibli's Spirited Away. Chase continued working in voice acting throughout her career, reprising the role of Lilo in various Lilo & Stitch sequels and spinoffs.

Chase's dual success in both family entertainment and horror made her a unique figure in Hollywood. The contrast between her warm, energetic voice work as Lilo and her unsettling portrayal of Samara showcased her range as a performer.

According to Hernandez, Chase had been admitted to a Los Angeles hospital earlier this month due to malnutrition before her condition worsened. In a GoFundMe page set up before her death, Hernandez described her struggles behind the scenes. "After a difficult childhood and a painful falling out with her family, Daveigh was bullied and struggled to find safety and happiness in downtown LA," he wrote. He added that he had promised to protect her and give her the love and comfort she deserved.

"Recently, everything changed. Daveigh was diagnosed with meningitis and several serious blood infections. Her condition has become critical, and the doctors have told me she may not have much time left," Hernandez said on the fundraising page, which had raised $1,300 of its $5,500 goal as of Wednesday evening.

News of her death spread rapidly across entertainment media, with tributes noting her impact on both Disney animation fans and horror enthusiasts.

cards.headline: Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson reunite for Apple TV comedy Brothers
cards.teaser: Apple TV set a September 23 premiere for the eight-episode series reuniting the True Detective co-stars.
cards.body:
Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson will reunite in Brothers, an eight-episode comedy series premiering September 23 on Apple TV. The show stars the actors as fictionalized versions of themselves, with their friendship thrown into crisis by unspecified events. Created by Lee Eisenberg, a producer on The Office, the series marks the first collaboration between McConaughey and Harrelson since their acclaimed work together on the first season of True Detective.

Apple TV released a first look at the series alongside the premiere date announcement. The show represents a shift to comedy for the pair, whose previous collaboration was the dark crime drama that earned both actors Emmy nominations in 2014.

cards.headline: Richard Linklater to receive career achievement honor at Zurich Film Festival
cards.teaser: The filmmaker will accept the Golden Eye award in person at the festival in September.
cards.body:
Richard Linklater will be honored with the Career Achievement Award at the Zurich Film Festival, receiving the Golden Eye for his body of work. The festival will present the award to Linklater on September 28 at the Filmpodium Zürich, where the filmmaker will appear in person to accept the honor.

The Zurich Film Festival described Linklater as one of the most influential auteur filmmakers of his generation. The American director is known for films including Boyhood, the Before trilogy, Dazed and Confused, and School of Rock, among others spanning more than three decades.

cards.headline: Betches launches first scripted comedy series Sisters
cards.teaser: The entertainment company will release its debut original scripted series this summer, based on a viral sketch series.
cards.body:
Betches, the entertainment company focused on millennial and Gen Z women, is launching its first original scripted comedy series called Sisters. The show expands the company's video content offerings beyond its existing shorter digital and sketch comedy formats.

Sisters is based on Betches' popular viral sketch series of the same name. The initial release will include three episodes, each running between 10 and 15 minutes long, rolling out this summer.

cards.headline: Kelsey Grammer to host The Great American Journey for NBC
cards.teaser: The series marking the 250th anniversary of US independence will premiere in August on NBC.
cards.body:
Kelsey Grammer will host The Great American Journey, a series produced by Hearst premiering August 22 on NBC in honor of the 250th anniversary of United States independence. The show will air on weekend mornings as part of NBC's The More You Know programming block and will be available to stream on Peacock and NBC.com.

The actor and producer will guide viewers through the anniversary programming. NBC has not released additional details about the format or specific content of the series beyond its connection to the milestone anniversary.

cards.headline: Panjaya.ai partners with Shortical on AI dubbing for microdramas
cards.teaser: The collaboration will localize mobile-first drama content into six languages using AI-powered tools.
cards.body:
Panjaya.ai and Shortical announced a strategic partnership Thursday to bring AI-powered localization to mobile-first microdrama content. The companies revealed the collaboration at the APOS conference in Bali. Under the agreement, Shortical's serialized drama output will be localized into Spanish, Portuguese, French, and German, with Japanese and Russian to follow.

The partnership targets audiences across multiple language markets through AI dubbing technology. Microdramas are short-form serialized video content designed for mobile viewing, a format that has gained popularity on social platforms.

cards.headline: Canadian animation showcases 11 competition films at Annecy Festival
cards.teaser: Canada has more than 11 films in competition at the French animation festival, with six additional titles in other programs.
cards.body:
Canada's animation industry has a strong presence at the Annecy Animation Film Festival in France, with more than 11 films competing in the main selection. Six additional Canadian titles appear in out-of-competition sections and special programs.

The National Film Board of Canada, Telefilm Canada, and the Canada Media Fund are supporting this showcase at Annecy, which includes its dedicated market MIFA. Canadian projects span diverse styles, from independent shorts to family entertainment, demonstrating the breadth of the country's animation sector on the global stage.

hero.headline: U.S. and Iran sign agreement to end war and reopen Strait of Hormuz
hero.body:
The United States and Iran have signed a memorandum of understanding to end their military conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route that handles approximately 20 percent of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas during peacetime. The agreement represents a significant shift in U.S. foreign policy toward the Middle East following months of escalating tensions.

President Trump defended the agreement, though it has drawn criticism from some who view it as returning to prewar conditions without addressing underlying disputes. Vice President JD Vance, who led U.S. negotiations, will hold a press briefing to address questions about the deal's terms and what concessions each side made to reach the agreement.

The Strait of Hormuz closure during the conflict created severe economic disruptions worldwide. The waterway's blockade contributed to spiraling fuel prices and global shortages of raw materials and fertilizer. The economic consequences extended far beyond energy markets, with countries in Asia heavily impacted and Europe facing significant challenges. Germany's largest economy announced it halved its 2026 growth forecast, while Greece introduced additional emergency aid for households and farmers struggling with rising fuel and living costs.

The closure has also left thousands of seafarers and commercial vessels stranded in the Gulf. According to the International Maritime Organization, approximately 20,000 seafarers and 2,000 ships remain unable to transit the waterway. The UN maritime agency has appealed for assistance for these stranded workers.

Recent weeks saw multiple escalations despite ongoing negotiations. Iran seized two cargo ships in the strait, claiming they attempted to exit covertly. Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaker of Iran's parliament and lead negotiator, stated that reopening the strait would be "impossible" while the U.S. and Israel continued what he characterized as ceasefire violations, including naval blockades.

Pakistan acted as mediator for talks intended to occur in Islamabad, but the negotiations collapsed. A Pakistani official told Reuters that extensive preparations had been made, but Iran never publicly accepted the invitation and the U.S. delegation never departed Washington, calling it an unexpected setback.

The conflict, which began on February 28, also created instability beyond the Strait of Hormuz. A second front opened between Israel and the Iranian proxy group Hezbollah in Lebanon, with ongoing strikes continuing despite a temporary ceasefire agreement.

Trump's approach marks a reversal from his first term, when he withdrew from a nuclear agreement with Iran that had limited its uranium enrichment program. That earlier withdrawal contributed to years of escalating tensions that culminated in the current conflict.

The agreement now faces the challenge of implementation while managing domestic political opposition and addressing concerns from regional allies about long-term stability.

cards.headline: Trump economic approval hits new low, trailing Biden's worst rating
cards.teaser: A new poll shows President Trump's economic approval at 33 percent, three points below former President Biden's lowest mark during his administration.
cards.body:
President Trump's approval rating for his handling of the economy has reached 33 percent, according to a new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll. This marks his lowest economic approval rating since taking office.

The figure is three percentage points below the lowest approval rating former President Biden received on economic matters during his presidency, when he hit 36 percent approval.

cards.headline: Democratic socialist Janeese Lewis George leads race for DC mayor
cards.teaser: Janeese Lewis George holds a double-digit lead in the District of Columbia mayoral race after opponent Kenyan McDuffie conceded Thursday morning.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

Lewis George, who serves on the D.C. City Council, holds about 53 percent of the vote in the race to succeed Mayor Bowser. McDuffie, her main opponent, conceded Thursday morning, though Decision Desk HQ has not yet officially called the race.

If Lewis George's lead holds, she will become the first democratic socialist to lead the nation's capital. The race drew national attention as a test of progressive politics in a major American city.

---

Note: The additional source material provided is about NASA and SpaceX, which is unrelated to the DC mayoral race. Per your instructions, I'm returning the original card text unchanged since the source does not pertain to this story.

cards.headline: Carville predicts Trump will leave office by spring 2027
cards.teaser: Democratic strategist James Carville suggested President Trump would depart office by next spring, citing anticipated midterm losses and the president's apparent fatigue.
cards.body:
Democratic strategist James Carville predicted that President Trump would depart office by spring 2027, suggesting that his life would become "miserable" following anticipated Democratic victories in the midterm elections. Carville based his forecast on the assumption that sweeping losses would make Trump's political circumstances untenable.

The strategist pointed to signs of Trump's dissatisfaction with the presidency, including statements about being bored with the Iran war and instances where he appeared to struggle staying awake during official duties.

cards.headline: Obama Presidential Center holds dedication ceremony in Chicago
cards.teaser: Former Presidents Obama, Biden, Clinton and Bush attended a ceremony marking the opening of the Obama Presidential Center.
cards.body:
The Obama Presidential Center held its dedication ceremony Thursday on Chicago's South Side, bringing together former President Obama, former first lady Michelle Obama, and other former presidents to mark the facility's opening.

The center represents a distinctive approach to presidential commemoration. The Obamas commissioned original works by 30 artists from diverse backgrounds—an unprecedented scale for a presidential library. Rather than a traditional library, the museum showcases Obama's legacy through both contemporary art and significant memorabilia, establishing the center as a major cultural addition to Chicago.

cards.headline: Gas prices drop below $4 per gallon following Iran deal
cards.teaser: The national average price of regular gasoline fell to about $3.99 after the U.S. and Iran signed their memorandum of understanding.
cards.body:
Gas prices in the U.S. fell below $4 per gallon for the first time in months on Thursday, according to reports tracking fuel costs. The decline came after the U.S. and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a critical passageway for global oil shipments.

The conflict between the U.S. and Iran had disrupted energy production and transportation across the Middle East, driving up fuel costs. With the strait's reopening, oil supply concerns eased, contributing to the drop in gas prices at the pump.

cards.headline: Vice President Vance to hold press briefing on Iran agreement
cards.teaser: Vice President Vance will brief reporters Thursday following the signing of the memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Iran.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance will hold a press briefing Thursday as the administration faces backlash over its Iran deal. This marks his second appearance at the White House podium while press secretary Karoline Leavitt is on maternity leave.

The agreement includes an end to fighting, a commitment that Iran will never develop nuclear weapons, and a $300 billion redevelopment package for Iran. The deal has drawn criticism for returning to prewar conditions, though the president has defended it publicly.
